In Magen Avraham, s.k. 8: that bread has no remedy. And at first glance it appears that if he has matzos dipped for challah in hand, he may take one of them to join in a basket with chametz bread and leave the matzah to separate from it on Chol HaMoed, as the Peri Chadash wrote in siman 497, that by means of basket-joining it is permitted to eat and continue, etc.; and so wrote Mekor Chaim (except that he disagrees with the Peri Chadash and holds that regarding eating and continuing, basket-joining does not help; and I already wrote on this above). And it appears at first glance that even though the Peri Chadash there holds specifically to join them from erev Yom Tov, but basket-joining on Yom Tov is forbidden, for it is considered fixing: here, where both have the amount for challah, one needs no basket-joining, only adjacency before him suffices, and this is not fixing even according to the Peri Chadash. But this is not so, for the view of the later authorities is that also regarding being contiguous one needs basket-joining, as Sefer HaTerumah and Semag wrote; and also according to the Rosh it was said only when he wants to separate immediately while they are adjacent before him; which is not so in this, where he wants to eat and continue and separate after Yom Tov: it is obvious that at least without basket-joining it does not help, even according to the Peri Chadash's explanation of Beit Yosef's words; and so Darkei Moshe understood Beit Yosef's words, as I wrote above. And since it is not permitted without joining, again it is fixing and forbidden according to the Peri Chadash. And so too it is proven from the words of Tosafos and the Mordechai, who found no remedy in basket-joining; and necessarily either it does not help for eating and continuing, or it is considered fixing and forbidden on Yom Tov. And if so there is no place to do so with this bread to fix it by means of basket-joining; for even if we say it is not considered fixing, necessarily we must say it does not help for eating and continuing, and either way it is forbidden. But there is still room to say, according to what I wrote above in the name of the Taz, that if the obligation comes by means of joining, it is permitted to eat and continue; and if so, if he has matzos from dough kneaded with less than the measure, he may join it in a basket and eat and continue and leave the matzah; and although the Peri Chadash forbids because of fixing, that is not the implication of Tosafos and the poskim, as Mekor Chaim wrote there, for they wrote to knead a small dough and join, etc. However, in truth it appears one can resolve the Peri Chadash's view, that he holds as I wrote above that what they wrote to knead dough means with the measure; and if so one needs no basket-joining, only adjacency, for the discussion is where he separates immediately. And with adjacency this does not appear like fixing, what he places adjacent to him; and what the poskim used the language of joining is explained below in the Magen Avraham, who explains 'and he combines them together' as adjacency. But it appears more regarding the Peri Chadash's view that even if we explain the language of Tosafos and the poskim plainly, that they hold like Sefer HaTerumah and Semag that one needs basket-joining regarding being contiguous, nevertheless there is no proof from there that it is permitted to do so on Yom Tov and it is not considered fixing; for there it is certainly permitted, for there is one that permits which was kneaded today, and with permission he separates from it, and thereby he can properly join it and exempt also the others incidentally; for in doing the act of joining there is here no act of permission at all, for there is not even a thought that the others be permitted by means of this joining, since he does not want to eat and continue; and if so this joining does not cause a permission of fixing at all; only afterward when he separates from the obligated matzah, from which he separates with permission, the others are exempted automatically; and in such a case where the permission does not come immediately at the time of joining, the Peri Chadash also agrees that there is no fixing prohibition in this. And so too it is clear from the Mordechai's language who wrote: because one may permit even if he rolled from erev Yom Tov, for they do no act with them but only think to exempt the others incidentally with that obligated matzah, end of his words; and his intent is as I wrote, that even if we explain 'and it will exempt the others' as vessel-joining as above, nevertheless the joining does not do the fixing, only the separation; and the separation has in the others no act, only thought alone, that he thinks at the time he separates from this obligated one; and that is why he compares it to a permitted device of deception; which is not so in the Peri Chadash's case, where by means of basket-joining he wants to eat and continue, for there is here nothing permitted at all, and all the doughs are equal in that he will eat and continue, and each would need separation from it and in it; and if he did an act with them and joined them together with intent to fix thereby so that at the end we need separate only from one and the exemption comes to the rest immediately at the time of joining, the Peri Chadash properly said that it is fixing. And I found in Sefer Rosh Yosef on the laws of Pesach, letter 22, who wrote like the Peri Chadash's words and with more explanation, and because of the length I did not copy it here. And according to this, if we adopt the Peri Chadash's view, even to join a matzah from dough of less than the measure, the joining is forbidden because of fixing. But it appears that even if we permit from the side of joining and not like the Peri Chadash, nevertheless this joining does not help at all to permit eating and continuing, just as there is no permit with two doughs of the measure; and although the Taz permits, that is specifically if neither of the two doughs has the measure in either one, for since neither became obligated of itself at all, and only joining together brought them to obligation, this is as if he rolled them as one and they became obligated together; if so the mind grants that since they are considered as one we say he eats and continues; but if one has the measure and became obligated of itself, even though the second does not have the measure and became obligated only because of the joining, nevertheless he cannot eat the entire dough upon which the obligation rested to separate from it; for even if he leaves over from the second that was joined, this does not discharge the first of its obligation. And it follows simply: since he joined upon it the second that did not have the measure and it became obligated by this joining, it is as if he added upon it at the time the dough was there and they were attached, which helps for eating and continuing; for if so also when each had the measure and he joined them together in a basket we should say likewise that it is as if they were attached together at the time of kneading; and this is indeed the Peri Chadash's view, that basket-joining is like kneading them together; but I already wrote that Darkei Moshe and the later authorities imply they disagree in this; and so too it implies from the plain words of Tosafos and the Mordechai; and although one can distinguish somewhat, that if one is less than the measure it is more fitting to say as if he kneaded them, since the large dough caused its obligation, it does not appear to me to distinguish thus. But it appears that even if we say like the Peri Chadash that joining helps for eating and continuing, nevertheless this is no remedy at all to join from the matzos; and from the outset of the law it is broken: since he needs to leave the matzah to separate challah and leftovers from it, if so he necessarily needs that it be in a manner permitted on Pesach, and it is impossible for him that it be mixed with the chametz, namely that he return them to their flour and they mix together; and it is explained in Yoreh Deah that anything he is particular about regarding its mixture does not join at all. And even according to what the Shach wrote in Nekudos HaKesef, siman 326, that specifically regarding joining to become obligated in challah, a thing one is particular about does not join, which is not so regarding being contiguous, where we are not concerned: even if he is particular about its mixture, basket-joining helps; nevertheless it appears that it does not help here, for in Nekudos HaKesef there he explained the reason for the distinction: specifically regarding joining, for the main obligation is that we view them as if they are one dough joined together, and he is particular about them not to join them together; but regarding being contiguous, where he separates from one upon its fellows, one need not that they be joined together; see there. And according to this it appears that this is only when he comes to separate now from one upon another and both are before us; we say that for being contiguous one need not that they be considered one dough; but if we come to permit by means of basket-joining to eat and continue and afterward separate, there is no place to say so unless we say that what he joined them in a basket is as if he rolled them and kneaded them together as the Peri Chadash wrote; and it is obvious that in this the law returns to be like the law of joining to become obligated: since we must say they became one dough, joining does not help when he is particular about its mixture. And even according to what he wrote there afterward in Nekudos HaKesef, that specifically with tamei and tahor where he is particular about touching even without mixing, nevertheless it is clear from his words that regarding joining to become obligated, if he is particular about the mixture it does not help even touching and biting; and therefore even if one is coarse bread or has saffron in it, joining does not help to become obligated: that is because one cannot say they became as one dough since he is particular about their mixture, even though he is not particular about touching; and if so it is obvious that regarding this, where each has the measure and he will eat and continue and afterward separate, one must specifically not be particular, for then there is place to say basket-joining helps as if he kneaded them; but if he is particular, so that one cannot say it is as if he kneaded them since he is particular about their mixture, it is obvious that even touching and biting do not help, as written in Nekudos HaKesef there regarding joining to become obligated, that all agree on this; and the same law regarding joining to eat and continue; and all the more so basket-joining alone does not help in this. And see in Mekor Chaim there who wrote that if we say it helps when he joins from the matzah, or even if he already separated from the matzos, there is a remedy that he ask [to annul] the separation, for one may ask for the need of Shabbos; see there. And this requires further study whether one may rule so l'chatchila, for the view of the Taz in Yoreh Deah siman 323 is that specifically when he regrets from the side of the giving itself for some reason he has, then he uproots the essence of the vow; which is not so where he has nothing to regret about the essence of the matter, only because it became mixed and he will have a loss, or because of fear of punishment: then asking does not help; see there. And if so it is obvious that here he has no reason to regret the separation of challah from the matzos except in order to fix the chametz; it appears that asking does not help according to the Taz. And also according to the view of Semag that the Rama cited, and likewise in Nekudos HaKesef who rejected the Taz's words, nevertheless it appears that they said so only there: even though he asks about this separation because of the mixture, nevertheless he immediately returns and separates another in its place; for then there is one who regrets with a whole heart because he returns and fixes the dough immediately; but in this, where it is impossible to return and separate immediately, and he will eat without separation relying on separating after Yom Tov, it appears that this does not help to uproot the separation retrospectively, to say that had he known a cause would occur requiring him to join from these matzos he would not have separated. And all the more so according to what Bach and Magen Avraham wrote according to the Tur's view in Orach Chaim, that l'chatchila one should not act relying on eating and continuing, etc., only specifically when he forgot; and all the more so if he has many matzos and from doughs each of which had the measure, so that he would need to leave a piece from each matzah: one should not permit him to ask about the separation and eat and leave over from each matzah, lest he not leave over from each one and what he separates afterward not help him, as explained above. For the law there is no practical difference in this, for without that there is no place for the remedy of joining the matzah, as explained above. And see in the Magen Avraham who wrote that one should not say: let him give the leftover to a non-Jew as a gift, and the non-Jew will return it to him after Pesach and he will separate challah, for one should be concerned that the non-Jew will eat it and it turns out he ate tevel; this implies that were it not for the concern that he will eat it, he would be permitted to do so, to give to a non-Jew as a gift even though he ate relying on separating from it; he is permitted to give it as a gift so that he can separate when [the non-Jew] returns it to him. And according to this it appears that if he has a partition where he can hide it until after Pesach, there is a remedy: let him give it to a non-Jew as a gift, and the non-Jew will return and give it to the Jew as a deposit without any liability at all, even for negligence; for in such a case it is permitted, as explained in siman 440; and it implies that even l'chatchila it is permitted to accept such a deposit before Pesach, as explained in Chok Yaakov there, s.k. 9. And one should not say one should be concerned lest he come during Pesach and demand that he give it to him: this is not so, for he can stipulate with him that he need not trouble himself to give it to him until after Pesach; and it is proper to do so for the need of Shabbos, for on Shabbos he is obligated to eat bread; and even if he has rich matzah that he is permitted to eat before the tenth hour, nevertheless on Shabbos he is obligated to eat bread upon which one is liable for Birkas HaMazon; see siman 471, s.k. 5.
It further appears that even if we say like Pri Chadash, that joining helps for eating progressively, this is still no remedy by joining from the matzot. The law is flawed from the start: since he must leave the matzah to separate challah from it and from the remnants, it must be in a form permitted on Pesach, and it cannot be mixed with the chametz by returning them to flour and mixing them together. It is explained in Yoreh Deah that anything whose mixture one is particular to avoid does not combine at all. Even according to what the Shach wrote in Nekudot HaKesef, siman 326, that only regarding combination to become obligated in challah does concern about mixture prevent combination, but regarding mukaf we are not concerned and basket-combination helps even if one is particular about mixing, here it appears that it does not help. There in Nekudot HaKesef he explained the distinction: for combination to create the primary obligation, we view them as if they are one joined dough, and he is particular not to join them; but for mukaf, where one separates from one for the others, they need not be joined as one. According to this, that applies only when one now comes to separate from one for another and both are visibly before us. But if we seek to permit through basket-combination that he eat progressively and separate afterward, there is no room to say this unless we say the basket-combination is as though he rolled and mixed them together, as Pri Chadash wrote. In that case the law returns to the law of combination to become obligated, and since they must be treated as one dough, combination does not help where he is particular about their mixture. Even according to what Nekudot HaKesef later wrote, that specifically with impure and pure dough one is particular about contact even without mixture, nevertheless it is clear from his words that regarding combination to become obligated, if one is particular about the mixture, even contact and touching do not help. Therefore even where one is coarse bread or contains saffron, combination does not help to create obligation because one cannot say they became one dough when he is particular about their mixture. If so, for this matter too, where each has the required measure and he wants to eat progressively and separate afterward, it must specifically be where he is not particular; then there is room to say basket-combination works as though they were mixed. But where he is particular, it cannot be as though mixed, and even contact and touching do not help, as written in Nekudot HaKesef regarding combination to obligate, and all agree to this. The same applies to combination for eating progressively, and all the more so mere basket-combination does not help.
See Mekor Chaim there, who wrote that if we say it helps when he combines from the matzah, or even if he already separated from the matzot, there is a remedy: he can ask to annul the separation, for one may ask for the sake of Shabbat; see there. It requires study whether one may rule so initially. The Taz in Yoreh Deah siman 323 holds that this helps specifically when he regrets the giving itself because of some reason, thereby uprooting the original vow, but where he has no regret about the essence of the matter, only because it became mixed and he will suffer loss or because of fear of punishment, inquiry does not help; see there. If so, here he has no reason to regret separating challah from the matzot except to repair the chametz, and it appears that inquiry would not help according to the Taz. Even according to the Semag brought by the Rama, and although Nekudot HaKesef rejected the Taz, it seems they said so only there, where although he asks about this separation because of the mixture, he immediately returns and separates another in its place; then he regrets wholeheartedly because he immediately repairs the dough. But here, where he cannot immediately separate again and will eat without separation relying on separating after Yom Tov, it appears this does not help to uproot the separation retroactively and say that had he known this circumstance would occur and he would need to join from these matzot, he would not have separated. All the more so according to what the Bach and Magen Avraham wrote in the Tur's view in Orach Chaim, that initially one should not act relying on eating progressively, except where he forgot. All the more so if he has many matzot from doughs each with the required measure, and he would need to leave a piece from each matzah, one should not permit him to ask about the separation, eat, and leave from each matzah, lest he not leave from each one and what he separates afterward will not help, as explained above. In practice this has no legal difference, for in any event there is no place for the remedy of joining matzah, as explained above.
See the Magen Avraham, who wrote that one should not say he can give what remains to a non-Jew as a gift, and the non-Jew will return it to him after Pesach and he will separate challah, because there is concern the non-Jew will eat it, and he would be eating tevel. This implies that were it not for the concern that he will eat it, one may give it to a non-Jew as a gift even though he ate relying on separating from it, and may give it as a gift so that he can separate when it is returned to him. According to this, if he has a partition where he can hide it until after Pesach, there is a remedy: he should give it to the non-Jew as a gift, and the non-Jew should return it to the Jew as a deposit without any responsibility at all, even for negligence. In such a case it is permitted, as explained in siman 440, and it implies that even initially one may accept such a deposit before Pesach, as explained in Chok Yaakov there, seif katan 9. One should not object that perhaps the non-Jew will come during Pesach and demand it, for he can stipulate with him that he need not trouble himself to give it to him until after Pesach. It is proper to do this for Shabbat need, for on Shabbat one is obligated to eat bread. Even if he has egg matzah that he may eat before the tenth hour, nevertheless on Shabbat he is obligated to eat bread over which one is obligated in birkat hamazon; see siman 471 seif katan 5.

kaf_hachayyim.he: ד) שם. אלא יקח באומד הדעת. ואם לוקח בכלי המיוחד למדה צריך להוסיף מעט או לפחות מעט. ב"ח. שכנה"ג בהגה"ט או' ב' א"ר או' א' פר"ח. מש"ז או' א' חמ"מ או' א' ח"א כלל פ"ה או' א' ליקוטי רימ"א שם או' א' קיצור ש"ע סי' צ"ח או' ט' מ"ב או ג':
kaf_hachayyim.en: 4) There. Instead, he should take an estimated amount. If he takes the flour with a vessel designated for measuring, he must add or subtract a small amount. Bach; Sheyarei Knesses HaGedolah, Hagahos HaTur, subsection 2; Eliyah Rabbah, subsection 1; Pri Chadash; Mishbetzos Zahav, subsection 1; Chemed Moshe, subsection 1; Chayei Adam, rule 85, subsection 1; Likutei Rima there, subsection 1; Kitzur Shulchan Aruch, siman 98, subsection 9; Mishnah Berurah, subsection 3.

mechaber.he: מותר לעשות בי"ט פתין גדולים ולא חיישי' שמתוך כך יבא לאפות יותר ממה שצריך:
mechaber.en: It is permitted to make large loaves on Yom Tov, and we are not concerned that through this one will come to bake more than what is needed.

beer_hagolah.en: A beraisa in Beitzah folio 22, and according to Beit Hillel.

beur_hagra.he:
אבל עיסה כו'. עבה"ג והביא הרי"ף ראיה שסוגיא דפ' משילין ל"ד א' כוותיה והרז"ה והרא"ש דחו ששם בחלת א"י אבל כאן בחלת ח"ל פליגי כיון שיכול לאכול ואח"כ להפריש והרמב"ן כ' חדא דא"כ הל"ל הלש בח"ל ועוד דתליא בפלוגתא דר"י ורשב"א בשבת קמ"ב במעלין הואיל ויכול ליתן עיניו כו':
אלא אוכל. וכ"ה בירוש' הג"מ ע"ש וכמ"ש שם נותן עיניו כו' ואפי' למאן דאסר שם כאן שא"צ אפי' ליתן עיניו מודה:
ואם רוצה כו'. ודמי למש"ש ח' ב' ל"ש אלא שאין כו' ובפ"ב מטבילין כלי ע"ג מימיו כו' נדה מערמת כו' וכ"ש כאן שאין רק מחשבה. וכמ"ש בפ"ג דפסחים הלש עיסה כו' ר"א לא תקרא שם כו' ואפי' עיסה חציה של א"י היה מותד אי לאו דאפשר לחלק בלישה משא"כ כאן וע"ש י"ב ב' א"ר יהודה לא נחלקו ב"ש וב"ה שמוליכין עם כו'. וכ"ש בכה"ג דאפי' אחרים מודו:
ס"ד המפריש כו'. מתני' פ"ג דפסחים וערש"י:
ס"ה מותר. כפי' תוס' שם ד"ה דנפישא כו':
beur_hagra.en:
But dough, etc. See Baal Hamaor; and the Rif brought a proof that the sugya of chapter Mashilin, folio 34a, follows him; and the Razah and the Rosh rejected [it], for there it is challah of Eretz Yisrael, but here regarding challah of chutz la'aretz they disagree, since one can eat and afterward separate; and the Ramban wrote: first, if so the Gemara should have said 'one who kneads in chutz la'aretz'; and further, it depends on the dispute of R' Yehuda and R' Shimon bar Abba in Shabbos folio 142 regarding raising [tithes], since one can set his eyes, etc.
Rather he eats. And so it is in the Yerushalmi; Hagahos Maimoniyos, see there; and as written there: he sets his eyes, etc.; and even according to the one who forbids there, here, where one does not even need to set his eyes, he agrees.
And if he wishes, etc. And it is similar to what is written there, folio 8b: it was stated only when there is no, etc.; and in chapter 2: one immerses a vessel upon its waters, etc.; a niddah uses a device, etc.; and all the more so here where there is only thought. And as written in Pesachim chapter 3: one who kneads dough, etc.; R' Eliezer: do not call a name, etc.; and even dough half of which is of a non-Jew would be permitted if it were not that one can divide at kneading, which is not so here. And see there folio 12b: R' Yehuda said: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not disagree that one brings with, etc. And all the more so in such a case, that even others agree.
Se'if 4. One who separates, etc. Mishnah, Pesachim chapter 3; and see Rashi.
Se'if 5. It is permitted. According to the explanation of Tosafos there, s.v. 'That is numerous,' etc.

eliyah_rabbah.he: [ח] ויש אומרים וכו'. וכן החמירו הב"ח וט"ז לכך כשנופלין זבובים בכוס יקח מעט משקה עמהם כשנוטלן ועל ט"ז קשה דלכאורה סותר עצמו במה שהסכים לתירוץ ראשון דבית יוסף עיין שם גם מה שהאריך לתמוה עיין בב"ח ותמצא מיושב, ופשוט דעל ידי כותים מותר:
eliyah_rabbah.en: [5] And some say, etc. And likewise the Bach and the Taz were stringent; therefore when flies fall into a cup, he should take a little liquid with them when he removes them. And upon the Taz it is difficult, for at first glance he contradicts himself in that he agreed to the first answer of Beit Yosef; see there; also regarding what he prolonged to wonder, see the Bach and you will find it resolved. And it is simple that by means of Cutheans it is permitted.

machatzit_hashekel.he: (ס"ק ה) ע"ג כו' צריך שינוי אחר וכתב בספר א"ר דאם מהפך דף השולחן ומרקד עליו זה מיקרי שינוי וכמ"ש רש"י ע"ש:
machatzit_hashekel.en: (s.k. 5) Upon, etc. Needs a different change. And Eliyah Rabbah wrote that if he inverts the table board and sifts upon it, this is called a change, as Rashi wrote; see there.

mishnah_berurah.he: {לב} ולא חיישינן שמתוך כך וכו' - ר"ל הואיל ואין בה טורח כ"כ כמו שיש בפת קטן בעריכת כ"א מהן וע"כ הו"א שיש לחוש שיאפה יותר ממה שצריך והיינו באופן שאסור וכגון בתנור גדול או בכמה פעמים דבתנור קטן ובפעם אחת אפילו לאפות יותר ממה שצריך לית לן בה מפני שהפת משתבח על ידי זה וכדלקמן סימן תק"ז ס"ו. וה"ה שמותר לו לאפות חררין דקים מאד אע"ג דטרח הרבה בעריכת ובלישת כל אחת ואחת:
mishnah_berurah.en: {32} And we are not concerned that from this, etc. Meaning: since there is not so much effort as there is with small loaves in forming each one, and therefore one might have thought to be concerned that he will bake more than he needs, and that is in a manner that is forbidden, such as in a large oven or in several batches; for in a small oven and in one batch, even baking more than he needs is no problem for us, because the bread improves thereby, as below in siman 507, se'if 6. And likewise it is permitted for him to bake very thin cakes, even though he toils much in forming and kneading each one.

peri_megadim.he: הלש עט״ז מלת אלא במ״ש הט״ז על דין דמהרי״א יראה ט״ס וצ״ל דמהרי״א לא כתב דבריו על דין זה היינו להוליכה חלה לכהן דלא זכר רק מהפרשה כו׳ עב״י אבל הב״ח מפרש דמהרי״א ז״ל קאי נמי אהולכה לכהן דאם גלגל עיסה מעי״ט בחלת א״י דאסור להפריש בי״ט ועבר והפריש בי״ט דאסור להוליכה לכהן בי״ט יע״ש וער״מ פכ״ג מה״ש הלכה ט״ו וביצה י״ז ב׳ משמע דבי״ט נמי אם הפריש תרומה כו׳ אין אוכל בו ביום א״כ פשיטא דאין מוליכה היום לכהן ואפשר בשוגג נמי אין מוליכה לכהן וצ״ע. ומ״ש על רש״ל היינו דרה״ר א״נ שרי ואנן קי״ל דתרומה אפי׳ הורמה מאמש נמי שרי להוליך בי״ט אין נ״מ בביתו ולמ״ש הב״ח נ״מ בשוגג והרים בי״ט וחלה כה״ג דאין מוליכה בי״ט אף בביתו י״ל דאסור ליתן לכהן באין רגיל אצלו ועא״ר ט׳. ומה שיש עושין חתיכה קטנה ומדבקין בלחם גדול וקורין לה שם חלה אין זה ניכר ומופרש ואסור בנילוש מעי״ט ופשוט הוא ועמ״א ואי״ה שם יבואר עוד:
peri_megadim.en: One who kneads. See Taz. The word “rather” in the Taz’s discussion of the ruling of Mahari Abuhav appears to be a scribal error. It should read that Mahari Abuhav did not write his ruling concerning this case, namely bringing challah to a kohen, for he mentioned only the separation of challah. See Beit Yosef. The Bach, however, explains that Mahari Abuhav also refers to bringing it to a kohen: if one rolled dough before Yom Tov in Eretz Yisrael, where it is forbidden to separate challah on Yom Tov, and he transgressed and separated it on Yom Tov, he may not bring it to a kohen on Yom Tov. See there. See Rambam, chapter 23 of Hilchos Shabbos, halachah 15, and Beitzah 17b, which imply that even on Yom Tov, if one separated terumah and the like, it may not be eaten that day. It is therefore obvious that one may not bring it to a kohen that day. Possibly, even if it was separated inadvertently, one may not bring it to a kohen. This requires study. What the Taz writes concerning Maharshal refers to a public domain. Alternatively, it is permitted because we rule that even terumah separated before Yom Tov may be brought to a kohen on Yom Tov. There is no practical difference when the kohen is in his house. According to the Bach, however, there is a practical difference where one inadvertently separated challah on Yom Tov: even in his own house he may not transfer it to a kohen. One may say that this applies when the kohen is not accustomed to receive gifts from him. See Eliyah Rabbah, seif katan 9. Some people take a small piece, attach it to a larger loaf, and then designate the small piece as challah. This is neither visibly separated nor set apart, and where the dough was kneaded before Yom Tov it is forbidden. This is obvious. See Magen Avraham; with Hashem’s help, the matter will be explained further there.

yad_ephraim.he: (במג"א ס"ק י"ב) ויצרפם יחד פי' שיהא סמוכות כו' הש"ע שם ביו"ד פסק כדעת הרא"ש אבל בנה"כ סי' שכ"ו הביא דעת סה"ת וסמ"ג והר"ש בחד שיטה שצריך צירוף סל גם לענין מוקף והארכתי בזה בספר שו"ת בית אפרים חלק א"ח סימן מ"ד ע"ש:
yad_ephraim.en: (In Magen Avraham s.k. 12) And combine them together — explanation: they should be in proximity, etc.; Shulchan Aruch there in Yoreh De'ah ruled like Ra'ash; but in Nekudot HaKesef siman 326 brought view Semak and Semag and Rash in one view that basket combining needed also for enclosing; I elaborated in responsa Beit Efraim part Orach Chaim siman 44, see there.

kaf_hachayyim.he: ה) שם. אלא יקח באומד הדעת. ולא חיישינן שמא ירבה על הצורך יו"ט דאפי' אם ירבה אין חשש בזה שהתנור מלא והפת נאפה יפה ואמנם בתנורים דידן שאין מדבקין הפת סביב התנור שמבואר לקמן סי' תק"ז סעי' ו' דאין לאפות יותר ממה שצריך ליו"ט מותר למדוד קמח ביו"ט מה"ט. ישי"ע או' א' אמנם מסתמיות דברי הטור והש"ע ושאר האחרונים משמע דאין לחלק בזה ובכ"ג אסור למדוד והטעם נראה לי דהא דאמרו דבתנורים שלנו אין לאפות יותר ממה שצריך ה"ד אם יודע בודאי שא"צ משא"כ כשלוקח באומד הדעת דאינו אלא ספק אם יקח מעט יותר זה לא נקרא אופה יותר ממה שצריך שאפשר שיאכל אותו מעט ועוד דהא גם באכילה אי אפשר לצמצם דלפעמים אוכל קימעה ופעמים יותר והוא ברור:
kaf_hachayyim.en: 5) There. Instead, he should take an estimated amount. There is no concern that he might take more than is needed for Yom Tov. Even if he takes more, there is no concern, because when the oven is full the bread bakes well. With our ovens, however, in which bread is not attached around the oven wall, it is explained below, siman 507, se'if 6, that one may not bake more than is needed for Yom Tov. Yeshuos Yaakov, subsection 1, therefore permits measuring flour on Yom Tov for this reason. Nevertheless, the unqualified wording of Tur, Shulchan Aruch, and the other later authorities implies that no distinction is made, and measuring is forbidden in every case. The reason appears to me to be that the statement that one may not bake more than needed in our ovens applies only when one knows with certainty that the additional amount is unnecessary. When one takes an estimated amount, however, it is only doubtful whether he will take a little more. This is not called baking more than necessary, because he might eat that small amount. Furthermore, it is impossible to precisely determine how much one will eat, for sometimes he eats little and sometimes more. This is clear.

mechaber.he: היה לו קמח או עיסה בשותפות עם העכו"ם אסור לאפותה ביום טוב אלא יחלקנה ויאפה את שלו:
mechaber.en: "If one had flour or dough in partnership with a non-Jew, it is forbidden to bake it on Yom Tov; rather, he should divide it and bake his own [portion]."

baer_heitev.he: לאפותה. אפי' בתנור אחד אע"פ שהפת משביח בכך. אחרונים:
baer_heitev.en: to the bake. In one oven, the map is barking. The Last:

beer_hagolah.en: A statement of Rav Chisda there, folio 21.

beur_hagra.he: ס"ו אסור כו'. עמ"ש בסי' תצ"ה ס"א בהג"ה:
beur_hagra.en: Se'if 6. It is forbidden, etc. See what I wrote in siman 495, se'if 1, in the gloss.

eliyah_rabbah.he: [ו] [לבוש] שהכל יוצא וכו'. ואם כן בקמח שלנו שכבר נרקד בריחיים ואין שם סובין אפשר דשרו לרקדו שנית (מגן אברהם ועיין סק"ב):
eliyah_rabbah.en: [6] [Levush] For everything comes out, etc. And if so, with our flour which has already been sifted at the mill and has no bran there, it is possible that they permit to sift it a second time (Magen Avraham; and see s.k. 2).

machatzit_hashekel.he: (ס"ק ו) ולהוליכן כו' בשבת. דבי"ט יוכל לאפותה. דהא מיירי במקום שהחלה טהורה ונאכלת לכהן:
machatzit_hashekel.en: (s.k. 6) And to bring them, etc. On Shabbos. For on Yom Tov he can bake it; for the discussion is in a place where the challah is tahor and is eaten by a kohen.

magen_avraham.he: אסור לאפותה. אפי' בתנור א' אף על פי שהפת משביח בכך כמ"ש סי' תק"ז ס"ו דהתם אוכל איזה פת שירצה א"נ אי מקלעי ליה אורחים אוכלים כל הפת משא"כ כאן (תו' יש"ש ב"ח) ע' סי' תקי"ב ס"א:
magen_avraham.en: It is forbidden to bake it. Even in one oven, even though the bread improves thereby, as I wrote in siman 507, se'if 6, for there one eats whichever bread one wishes; alternatively, if guests happen upon him, they eat all the bread; which is not so here (Tosafos; Yam Shel Shlomo; Bach). See siman 512, se'if 1.

mishnah_berurah.he:
{לג} אסור לאפותה - היינו בעיסה ובקמח אסור אפילו ללוש ולא דמי לבהמה שחציה של ישראל וחציה של עכו"ם דמותר לשחטה ביו"ט כנ"ל בסי' תצ"ח סי"א דשאני התם דא"א לכזית בשר בלא שחיטה אבל הכא הא אפשר לחלק מקודם ויטריח בחלקו לבד:
{לד} ביו"ט - היינו אפילו בתנור אחד ואפילו בתנור קטן דפסק המחבר לקמן בסי' תק"ז ס"ו דמותר לאפות תנור מלא פת אע"פ שא"צ אלא לפת א' והיותר ישאר לחול מפני שהפת נאפה יפה בזמן שהתנור מלא דשאני התם שכל הפת של ישראל ורשות בידו לאכול כל אחד ואחד או זה או זה ועוד דלמא מקלעי ליה אורחים וחזו כולהו ליו"ט אבל הכא דחציו של עכו"ם דמוכרח להשאיר חלקו ואם כן הוא טורח בלישה ואפייה של עיסת העכו"ם בשביל הוספת שבח הפת שלו בעלמא ואסור:
mishnah_berurah.en:
{33} It is forbidden to bake it. That is, with dough; and with flour it is forbidden even to knead. And it is unlike an animal half of which belongs to a Jew and half to a non-Jew, which one may slaughter on Yom Tov, as above in siman 498, se'if 11; for that case is different, since it is impossible [to get] a kezayis of meat without slaughter; but here it is possible to divide beforehand and toil only in his own share.
{34} On Yom Tov. That is, even in one oven, and even in a small oven; for the Mechaber ruled below in siman 507, se'if 6, that it is permitted to bake a full oven of bread even though he needs only one loaf and the rest will remain for a weekday, because the bread bakes well when the oven is full; for that case is different, since all the bread belongs to the Jew and he has authority to eat each one, this or that; and further, perhaps guests will happen upon him and all are fit for Yom Tov. But here, where half belongs to a non-Jew, he is forced to leave that share; and if so he toils in kneading and baking the non-Jew's dough merely for the added improvement of his own bread in general, and it is forbidden.

peri_megadim.he: יכול עט״ז לא הבינותי זה דרש״י פי׳ כן ביצה ט׳ א׳ דאף מעי״ט לא היה בכלל הגזירה ע׳ תוס׳ שם אבל לדידן דוקא חלת ח״ל דאוכל ומפריש אח״כ אבל להפריש בי״ט מה שגלגל בעי״ט אסור וצ״ע. ואפשר סברתו חלת א״י קיל טפי וגלגל מעי״ט ושכח מפריש בי״ט כרבה דלא הוי בכלל הגזירה ואבוה דשמואל חולק רק בח״ל ובל״ז פירי דטבילי האידנא בח״ל איירי וכ״ז צ״ע בזה:
peri_megadim.en: He may. See Taz. I did not understand this, for Rashi explains in Beitzah 9a that even when the dough was prepared before Yom Tov, the case was never included in the decree. See Tosafot there. According to our ruling, however, this applies specifically to challah outside Eretz Yisrael, where one may eat first and separate challah afterward. To separate on Yom Tov from dough rolled before Yom Tov is forbidden. This requires study. Perhaps his reasoning is that challah in Eretz Yisrael is more lenient in this respect: if one rolled the dough before Yom Tov and forgot, he may separate challah on Yom Tov in accordance with Rabbah, since it was not included in the decree, while the father of Shmuel disagrees only regarding challah outside Eretz Yisrael. Moreover, the discussion of produce that is tevel nowadays concerns produce outside Eretz Yisrael. All of this requires study.

yad_ephraim.he: (בש"ע ויצרפם יחד) ואם גלגל שני עיסות מעיו"ט שאין בכ"א שיעור חלה ונצטרפו יחד ביו"ט לכאורה היה מקום לומר דכיון שהחיוב חלה לא היה קודם יו"ט אלא עתה ביו"ט בא החיוב לפי שנצטרפו ונתחייבו מותר להפריש ביו"ט כמו בלש ביו"ט. אך נראה לפי הטעם שכ' רש"י דאף על גב דאסור להפריש ביו"ט לפי שהיה יכול להפריש מאתמול שאני הכא שהרי מותר לגלגלה ולאפותה כדי לאכול פת חמה לא גזרו בי' רבנן והביאו הט"ז. אם כן משמע דבלאו הך טעמא שמותר לגלגל היום לא היה מותר אעפ"י שהחיוב בא היום ולא היה יכול להפרישו מאתמול ולא דמי לתרומות ומעשרות דאיטבלי מאתמול דמכל מקום אסור שהיה לו ללוש מאתמול ולהפריש רק כיון דמותר לו להשהות הלישה עד היום משום לאכול פת חמה לא גזרו בי' ואם כן בשני עיסות פחות מכשיעו' שלש מעיו"ט אף שהחיוב בא היום מ"מ הרי יכול לצרפם מאתמול והיתר לאכול פת חמה לא שייך הכא אין להפריש חלה ביום טוב. אך בביצה דף י"ב ע"ב קאמר אהא דמוללין מלילות ביום טוב אמרי' אם כן מצינו תרומה שזכאי בהרמתה כו' ולר"י בר' יהודה נמי משכחת לה כגון שהכניס לעשות עיסה ונמלך למוללן ביו"ט דטבלא ביומי' ופירש"י שמוללן ביו"ט מפריש תרומה ביו"ט עיין שם מבואר דאף דליכא טעמא דפת חמה מותר. ואפשר דרש"י לא כ"כ אלא ליתן טעמ' למ"ד גלגל עיסה בעיו"ט מפריש עליו ביו"ט משום דחלה ליתא בגזרת אין מגביהין כיון שמותר ללוש ביו"ט משום פת חמה וע"כ טבלי ביו"ט ומפריש חלה לא גזרו בה אבל למ"ד דגלגל עיסה בעי"ט באמת אין מפריש רק אם גלגל ביו"ט תו לאו מהאי טעמא אתינין עלה אלא משום דלא שייך בי' שהיה לו להפרישה מאתמול דהאידנא אתי חיובא שפיר מפרש עלה וא"ש ההיא דמלילות שהוא זכאי בהרמתה כיון שלא היה מקום חיוב קודם יו"ט כלל. ומ"מ נראה דנ"ד דנצטרפו היום בסל ל"ד להתם כיון שצריך עכשיו לעיסה ולכן הוא מולל מלילות וכיון שמחמת זה מותר לעשות היום חיוב דתרומה ממילא קאתי האידנא ולכן הוא זכאי גם כן באמירתה. מה שאין כן בנ"ד שמה שהיא צורך אכילה כבר עשוי מאתמול ולא היה צריך להפריש חלה כלל ומה שנתחדש היום שצריך להפריש חלה הוא סיבת הצירוף שלא היה צריך לעשותו היום כלל אין היתר בדבר מחמת שהחיוב בא היום. ומצאתי בחק יעקב סימן תצ"ז ס"ק ט' שכ' דאפשר דמותר כה"ג לצרף ביו"ט ולהפריש כיון דלא טביל עד השתא וכמשמעות הש"ס בהא דמוללין מלילות כו' עיין שם. ובא"ר שם חולק עליו וכת' דמדברי התוספות והאגודה וכלבו משמע דאף כשהחיוב בא על ידי צירוף אסור להפריש ביו"ט ואף שלפענ"ד אין הכרח מ"מ כן עיקר לדינא. ועיין בב"י סימן רי"ז שכ' על דברי התוספות דביצה והמרדכי ומשמע דהיינו כשלא נצטרפו יחד בסל וע"ש בד"מ וב"ח ופר"ח ובמק"ח כ' שא"ל שאם אין בכ"א כשיעור והחיו' בא על ידי צירוף סל שפי' יכול להיות אוכל והולך כמ"ש הט"ז וכ"כ עוד מחברים ולפי דעת הח"י שחולק בזה על הט"ז שם יש לומר לפי שיטתו דאם נצטרף ביו"ט יכול להפריש א"כ יש לו' דר"ל דבכה"ג שהחיוב על ידי צירוף הסל ומצטרף ביו"ט אין צריך לתקנות אלו דשפיר יכול להפריש ביו"ט אך לשונו לא משמע כן ועיין בח"י שם סק"ו במ"ש שם ומ"מ בדיעבד כו' אבל אם אין בעיסות כשיעו' ואכל אף בדיעבד לא מהני הפרש' אח"כ כיון דלא צירפם יחד א"כ לא נתחייבה בחלה כלל א"כ שייר מכ"א וא' חתיכה ויצרפם עכ"ל ולא ידענא מה קאמר מר דהא כיון דלא צירפה לא נתחייבו כלל ובהיתרא קאכיל ולמה יצטרך להפריש חתיכה חתיכה וצ"ע:
yad_ephraim.en: (In Shulchan Aruch 'and combine them together') If he rolled two doughs from erev Yom Tov without challah measure in each and they joined on Yom Tov — apparently one could say since challah obligation was not before Yom Tov but now on Yom Tov obligation came by joining, permitted to separate on Yom Tov like kneading on Yom Tov. But it appears per Rashi's reason: although forbidden to separate on Yom Tov because could have separated yesterday — not here since permitted to roll and bake for hot bread — rabbis did not decree; if so without this hot-bread reason permitted to roll today even though obligation came today and could not separate yesterday — not comparable to terumot and ma'asrot that became tevel yesterday, for anyway forbidden to knead yesterday and separate, only since permitted to delay kneading until today for hot bread they did not decree; if so two doughs less than measure kneaded erev Yom Tov — although obligation came today, can combine from yesterday and hot-bread permission does not apply here — no separating challah on Yom Tov. But Beitzah daf 12b on plucking sheaves on Yom Tov: if so we find terumah entitled to its separation, etc.; for Rabbi Yehuda too you find case entering to make dough, decided to pluck on Yom Tov — barrel in days, Rashi: plucking on Yom Tov separates terumah on Yom Tov, see there clear even without hot-bread reason permitted. Perhaps Rashi only gives reason for one who rolls dough on Yom Tov separates on Yom Tov due to challah lacking in decree 'we do not separate' since permitted to knead on Yom Tov for hot bread therefore became tevel on Yom Tov and separate challah — they did not decree; but for one who rolls dough truly separates only if rolled on Yom Tov — not from this reason; rather because not applicable that should have separated yesterday — obligation now comes properly separates; not like sheaves case where entitled since no obligation place before Yom Tov. Still DNA joined today in basket to death leaf needs dough now plucks from nights and because of this permitted today terumah obligation comes now therefore entitled also to state. Not like our case where eating need already done yesterday, never needed separate challah, what renewed today needing challah is combining cause not needed today — no permission because obligation came today. Found in Chok Yaakov siman 497 s.k. 9 wrote perhaps permitted thus combine on Yom Tov and separate since not tevel until now like gemara plucking sheaves, see there. Ateret Tzvi disputes and writes from Tosafot, Agudah, Kol Bo implies even when obligation via combining forbidden separate on Yom Tov; though in my humble opinion not required, nevertheless main for ruling. See Beit Yosef siman 217 on Tosafot Beitzah and Mordechai implies when not joined in basket; see Darchei Moshe, Bach, Pri Chadash, Kaf HaChayim wrote: if neither has measure and obligation via basket combining meaning can eat-and-continue as Taz wrote; more authors; per Chayei Adam disputing Taz there, per his view if joined on Yom Tov can separate — then means when obligation via basket combining and joined on Yom Tov no need these remedies, may separate on Yom Tov; but wording does not imply; see Chayei Adam s.k. 6 there; nevertheless b'dieved, etc.; but if doughs lack measure and he ate — even b'dieved separation afterward fails since did not combine — not obligated challah at all — left from each one piece and combine, end quote; I do not know what master says, for since did not combine not obligated at all and eats in permission — why need separate piece by piece, requires further study.

kaf_hachayyim.he: ו) שם הגה. ומותר ליקח קמח מן הכלי וכו' ר"ל שא"צ לערות הקמח מהכלי לתוך העריבה אלא מותר ליקחו בידיו מהכלי אעפ"י שעושה גומא בקמח הנשאר בכלי שאין עשיית גומא שייך לא בקמח ולא בפירות שהרי איסור עשיית גומא אינה אלא משום בונה ואין בנין אלא בקרקע או במחובר לקרקע. ר"ז או' ב' מק"ק סי' כ"ג או' ב' מ"ב או' ד':
kaf_hachayyim.en: 6) There, in the gloss. It is permitted to take flour from the vessel, etc. This means that one need not pour the flour from the vessel into the kneading trough, but may take it from the vessel with his hands. This is permitted although he makes a depression in the flour remaining in the vessel. The prohibition against making a depression applies neither to flour nor to fruit. That prohibition is due only to building, and building applies only to the ground or something attached to the ground. Shulchan Aruch HaRav, subsection 2; Mikraei Kodesh, siman 23, subsection 2; Mishnah Berurah, subsection 4.

mechaber.he: אם יש לאדם הרבה פת נקייה אינו אופה פת אחרת אלא א"כ יש לו בני בית שרגיל להאכילם פת הדראה אבל אם יש לו פת הדראה הרבה יכול לאפות פת נקייה:
mechaber.en: If a person has much fine bread, he may not bake other bread unless he has household members whom he regularly feeds coarse bread. But if he has much coarse bread, he may bake fine bread.

beer_hagolah.he:
סמ"ק והר"ן בפט"ז דשבת בשם התוספות מברייתא דהציל פת נקיה וכו'
הרא"ש שם
beer_hagolah.en:
Semak and the Ran in chapter 16 of Shabbos in the name of Tosafos, from the beraisa of 'If one saved fine bread,' etc.
The Rosh there.

eliyah_rabbah.he: [ז] על גבי שולחן וכו'. ומי שדרכו לנפות בחול על גבי שולחן צריך שינוי אחר (מגן אברהם) וטוב להפך השולחן:
eliyah_rabbah.en: [7] Upon a table, etc. And one whose way on a weekday is to sift upon a table needs a different change (Magen Avraham); and it is good to invert the table.

machatzit_hashekel.he: (ס"ק ז) אוכל כו' עבי"ד דאסור לאכול עד שיפריש תחילה:
machatzit_hashekel.en: (s.k. 7) He eats, etc. See Yoreh Deah, that it is forbidden to eat until he first separates.

magen_avraham.he: אם יש וכו'. משמע בתו' דשבת דף קי"ז דמותר לכתחלה לאפות פת הדראה ואח"כ פת נקיה:
magen_avraham.en: If there is, etc. It is implied in Tosafot to Shabbat, page 117, that it is permitted at the outset to bake coarse bread and afterward fine bread.

mishnah_berurah.he:
{לה} הרבה פת נקיה - שמספיק לו לכל היום:
{לו} אינו אופה וכו' - בין פת נקיה ובין פת הדראה [היינו פת קיבר] דהא יש לו פת נקיה שטוב לו יותר לאכילתו ונראה לי דדוקא אם הפת האחר הוא מאותו המין אבל אם הוא מין אחר אפילו גרוע מזה כגון שהפת שלו הוא פת חטים והוא רוצה לאפות פת דגן שרי:
{לז} פת אחרת - ואם ניחא ליה בפת חמה והפת נקיה נאפה מאתמול שרי לאפות אפילו פת הדראה:
{לח} ב"ב שרגיל וכו' - ומשמע דבאינם רגילים אלא שבפעם הזאת רוצה להאכילם אסור:
{לט} אבל אם יש לו וכו' - עיין במ"א דמותר לכתחלה לאפות פת הדראה ואח"כ פת נקיה. ודוקא אם רוצה לאכול הפת הדראה אבל אם כונתו להערים שיותר לחול בודאי אסור:
mishnah_berurah.en:
(א) It's a lot of clean-up that is enough for him all day:
(2) {He} does not bake, etc. - between a clean pate and a draya pate [that is, a Kiber pate] he has a clean pate that is better for him to eat and it seems to me that if the other pate is of the same species but if it is a different species it is even worse than that, such as his pate is a tatim pate and he wants to bake a sherry grain pate:
(ג) Another path – and if you have a warm and dry map, Napa from yesterday’s Sri Laf has even been visible:
(4) {Lach} 22 Shargil, etc. - and it means that they are normal, except that this time he wants to feed them, it is forbidden:
(5) {Lat} But if he has, etc. - refer to the MA Domtar to begin with baking a clean mouth and then a clean mouth. And precisely if you want to eat a portion of the drayah, but if it was called to trick more than sand, it is certainly not allowed:

peri_megadim.he: ומותר עט״ז עמ״א אות יו״ד בזה איסורא דרביע עליה ואי״ה שם יבואר עוד:
peri_megadim.en: And it is permitted. See Taz and Magen Avraham, seif katan 10, regarding an item upon which a prohibition presently rests. With Hashem’s help, the matter will be explained further there.

kaf_hachayyim.he:
ז) שם בהגה. ומותר ליקח קמח וכו' ומשמע שבחול ועפר שייך גומא אם הוא קשה אפי' תלוש מן הקרקע וא"כ מה שתוחבין ביו"ט נר של שעוה לתוך החול הקשה או כשנוטלין אותו ממנו לאו שפיר עבדי דעושה גומא דהר"ן כתב דאסור להטמין ביצה בעפר תיחוח אלא א"כ תחוח כ"כ כשהוא נותן הביצה ע"ג עפר נכנסת מאליה בתוכה, וכ"כ התו' אבל בשבת דף קי"ג משמע דמותר להוציא דבר התחוב אעפ"י שעושה גומא. מ"א סי' תצ"ח ס"ק ל"ב יעו"ש ועיין לעיל סי' תצ"ח או' קנ"ב ולקמן סי' תקי"ד או' מ"ד:
ז) שם. בהגה. אעפ"י שעושה גומא בקמח. אבל ליקח אפר מהכירה אם עושה גומא אסור ומדברי התו' והרא"ש משמע דשרי ואין להקל בדבר. פר"ח. ועיין לעיל סי' תצ"ח סעי' ט"ו ובדברנו לשם בס"ד:
kaf_hachayyim.en:
7) There, in the gloss. It is permitted to take flour, etc. This implies that making a depression applies to sand and earth when the material is hard, even if detached from the ground. Accordingly, those who on Yom Tov insert a wax candle into hard sand, or remove it from there, do not act properly, because they make a depression. Ran writes that it is forbidden to bury an egg in loose earth unless the earth is so loose that when the egg is placed upon it, the egg enters by itself. Tosafos write likewise. Shabbos 113a, however, implies that one may remove an inserted object even though this makes a depression. Magen Avraham, siman 498, subsection 32. See there. See above, siman 498, subsection 152, and below, siman 514, subsection 44.
7) There, in the gloss. Although he makes a depression in the flour. It is forbidden, however, to take ashes from a stove if doing so makes a depression. The words of Tosafos and Rosh imply that it is permitted, but one should not be lenient in this matter. Pri Chadash. See above, siman 498, se'if 15, and our words there, with Heaven's help.

mechaber.he: אסור לעשות שאור ביום טוב אלא ע"י שינוי מפני שהיה אפשר לעשותו מבעוד יום:
mechaber.en: It is forbidden to make leaven on Yom Tov except with an alteration, because it was possible to make it while it was still day [before Yom Tov].

eliyah_rabbah.he: [ח] ולהוליכה וכו'. וכן בשבת כשנאפית דהא מוקצה הוא ועיין בט"ז מה שתמה על רש"ל דמתניתין פרק ד' דדמאי הוא כבית שמאי אבל לבית הלל מותר ליתן לו בביתו ועל כן לא הזכירו הפוסקים מזה כלל, עד כאן, ותימא לתמיהתו הא בפסקי תוס' פרק קמא דביצה דוקא ברגיל אצלו מותר ליתן לו בביתו, וכן כתב הרמב"ם פרק כ"ג מהלכות שבת דין ט"ז, ואי נחלק בין שבת ליום טוב אם כן תיקשי על הר"ש וירושלמי דדמאי שם ודו"ק, ואפילו אין רשות הרבים בין בית כהן לביתו משמע דאסור ודעת הט"ז דאף ברשות הרבים הא מותר לישראל להוציאה לצורך כהן כמו דמותר בטילטול, עד כאן, ולא נהירא דדמי לסימן תקי"ח סעיף ג' דאסור להוציא לצורך כותים וטילטול דאוכלים שאני וכן משמע בסימן תקי"ב סעיף ג' במאכל בהמה:
eliyah_rabbah.en: [8] And to bring it, etc. And likewise on Shabbos when it is baked, for it is muktzeh; and see in the Taz what he wondered upon Maharshal, that the mishnah in Demai chapter 4 is according to Beit Shammai, but according to Beit Hillel it is permitted to give him in his house, and therefore the poskim did not mention this at all, until here. And it is surprising regarding his wonder, for in Piskei Tosafos, first chapter of Beitzah, specifically when he is regularly accustomed with him it is permitted to give him in his house; and so wrote the Rambam, Hilchos Shabbos chapter 23, law 16. And if we distinguish between Shabbos and Yom Tov, then it is difficult against the Rash and the Yerushalmi of Demai there; and be precise. And even if there is no public domain between the kohen's house and his house, it implies it is forbidden. And the view of the Taz is that even in a public domain it is permitted for a Jew to take it out for the need of a kohen, just as moving is permitted, until here. And this is not clear, for it is similar to siman 518, se'if 3, that it is forbidden to take out for the need of Cutheans; and moving of foods is different; and so it implies in siman 512, se'if 3, regarding animal food.

machatzit_hashekel.he:
(ס"ק ח) ולמחר כו' שמא יבקע הנוד. דתנן בדמאי והובא בעירובין דף ל"ז וביתר מקומות. הלוקח יין מבין הכותים קודם שגזרו על יינם. ולאשר חשודים על לפני עור לא תתן מכשול. ואין מפרישים תרומות ומעשרות ממה שמוכרים לאחרים. והוא ע"ש ואין לו כלים להפריש לתוכן תרומות ומעשרות. ס"ל לר"מ דא"ל ברירה לכן מותר לו' שני לוגין שאני עתיד להפריש (דרך משל אם סך הכל מאה לוגין) הן תרומה (כשיעור עין בינוני) וכן אומר על שאר המעשרות אשר צריך להפריש ועל סמך זה מותר לשתות מהיין בשבת והנשאר לבסוף הוברר למפרע שהוא התרומה ומעשר. ור' יודא פליג ואמר אפי' אי אמרי' ברירה מ"מ הא א"ל שמא יבקע הנוד וישפך היין שיהי' תרומה ומעשר ונמצא למפרע שתה טבל. ור"מ לא חייש להכי דהוי מילתא דלא שכיח אבל כאן אף דבשעת אכילה לא עביד איסורא מ"מ לבסוף ודאי לא יוכל להפריש חלה דהא צריך לבער לכ"ע אסור דיאכל טבל למפרע:
דהא אסור ליתן על תנאי כמ"ש לעיל סי' תמ"ח סעיף ג':
שמא יאכלנו כו' והוי דומיא דשמא יבקע הנוד. והכא לכ"ע חיישינן דמלתא דשכיח שהגוי יאכלנו:
machatzit_hashekel.en:
(s.k. 8) And tomorrow, etc. Perhaps the skin bottle will burst. For we learned in a mishnah regarding demai, and it is brought in Eruvin folio 37 and in other places: one who buys wine from among the Cutheans before they decreed upon their wine; and since they are suspect regarding 'before a blind person you shall not place a stumbling block,' and they do not separate terumos and maasros from what they sell to others; and he is on the way and has no vessels into which to separate terumos and maasros. R' Meir holds that we say bereirah; therefore it is permitted for him to say: two logs that I am destined to separate (for example, if the total is one hundred logs) are terumah (at the amount of an average eye), and likewise he says regarding the other tithes that he needs to separate; and relying on this it is permitted to drink from the wine on Shabbos, and what remains at the end is clarified retrospectively that it is the terumah and maaser. And R' Yehuda disagrees and says: even if we say bereirah, nevertheless one should not say [so], perhaps the skin bottle will burst and the wine that was to be terumah and maaser will spill, and it turns out retrospectively that he drank tevel. And R' Meir is not concerned for this, for it is an uncommon matter. But here, even though at the time of eating he does not commit a prohibition, nevertheless at the end he certainly will not be able to separate challah, for he must dispose [of chametz]; therefore according to all it is forbidden, lest he eat tevel retrospectively.
For it is forbidden to give on condition, as written above in siman 448, se'if 3.
Perhaps he will eat it, etc. And it is similar to 'perhaps the skin bottle will burst.' And here according to all we are concerned, for it is a common matter that the non-Jew will eat it.

mishnah_berurah.he:
{מ} אסור לעשות שאור - להחמיץ העיסה:
{מא} מפני שהיה אפשר וכו' - שכל כך יפה הפת שנעשה שאור שלו מבע"י כמו כשנעשה ביומו ודע דסברא זו הוא לכאורה כפי דעה ב' בסימן תצ"ה בהג"ה דגם באוכל נפש גופיה מחמרינן באינו מפיג טעם כלל אם עושהו מעיו"ט ועיין מ"ש שם בבה"ל לחלק קצת בזה:
mishnah_berurah.en:
(א) It is forbidden to make light to miss the cover:
(41) Because it was possible, etc. — that the bread turned out so well that its chametz is from erev Yom Tov as when made on its day; and know that this reasoning is apparently per the second view in siman 495 in the gloss that even in ochel nefesh itself we are stringent where it does not nullify taste at all if one makes it from erev Yom Tov; and see what is written there in Biur Halachah to distinguish somewhat in this.

peri_megadim.he: והוא עט״ז עי״ד שכ״ז ולעיל תנ״ז חלת ח״ל חלת האור נשרפת אפי׳ נילוש במי ביצים וכדומה שלא הוכשר מעולם למ״ד חייב בחלה נשרפת דלית כהן טהור האידנא אין נוהגין כו׳ א״כ הדין נוהג בטהורה ג״כ דימתין עד הלילה וער״מ פ״ג מהל׳ י״ט ה״ח בזה ויש ליזהר שלא ישרוף רק יניחנה עד הערב והנה בשאר י״ט עושין כן ולאפותה י״ל אסור לכ״ע דאפשר למפלג בלישה עי׳ אות ז׳ ובפסח א״א יאפה עסי׳ תנ״ז ואי״ה במ״א אות יו״ד יבואר עוד:
peri_megadim.en: And this applies. See Yoreh Deah 327 and above, siman 457. Challah outside Eretz Yisrael, which is challah consigned to the fire, must be burned even if the dough was kneaded with egg water or the like and was never susceptible to ritual impurity. According to the opinion that such dough is obligated in challah, it is burned because no ritually pure kohen is available nowadays. Since the custom not to burn it does not apply, the same law should apply even where the challah itself is ritually pure: one should wait until nightfall. See Rambam, chapter 3 of Hilchos Yom Tov, halachah 8, regarding this. One must be careful not to burn it on Yom Tov, but to leave it until evening. On other festivals this is what is done. Baking it, however, appears forbidden according to all opinions, because one could have divided the dough before kneading. See seif katan 7. On Pesach, where leaving it unbaked is impossible, it should be baked; see siman 457. With Hashem’s help, this will be explained further in Magen Avraham, seif katan 10.

kaf_hachayyim.he: ח) [סעיף ב'] אין מרקדין הקמח וכו' מפני שהיא מלאכה הנעשית לזמן מרובה. הר"ן. והיש"ש כתב כמ"ש התו' ריש ביצה דכל המלאכות אין מותרות אלא מלישה ואילך מ"א סק"ב. ועיין לעיל סי' תצ"ה או' כ"ד שכבר כתבנו הפלוגתא בזה במלאכות דקודם הלישה אם אסורה מדאו' או מדרבנן יעו"ש. ועיין א"א או' ב' שכתב דלטעם הראשון דגזור אטו מרקד לזמן מרובה אף אם א"א מעיו"ט אסור כבצירה וטחינה יעו"ש. וכ"פ הר"ז או' ג' מ"ב או' ה' ועיין לעיל סי' תצ"ה או' כ"א:
kaf_hachayyim.en: 8) [Seif 2] One may not sift flour, etc. The reason is that this is a type of work normally performed for a long-term need. Ran. Yam Shel Shlomo writes, in accordance with Tosafos at the beginning of Beitzah, that the only food-preparation labors permitted on Yom Tov are those from kneading onward. Magen Avraham, seif katan 2. See above, siman 495, letter 24, where we already wrote the dispute whether labors performed before kneading are prohibited by Torah law or rabbinically; see there. See Eshel Avraham, letter 2, who writes that according to the first reason, that sifting was prohibited lest one sift for a long-term need, it remains prohibited even if it could not have been done before Yom Tov, just like harvesting and grinding; see there. So ruled Shulchan Aruch HaRav, letter 3, and Mishna Berurah, letter 5. See above, siman 495, letter 21:

mechaber.he: אפילו נשחטה הבהמה מערב יום טוב מותר להפריש המתנות בי"ט:
mechaber.en: Even if the animal was slaughtered on the eve of Yom Tov, it is permitted to separate the gifts on Yom Tov.

beer_hagolah.en: Mahari Abuhab in the name of the Rashba.

beur_hagra.he: ס"ט אפי'. עמ"א דלא כו' ועוד דמפורשות כו' וכ"ה בב"י בשם מהרי"א. וגמ' ערוכה היא שם י"ב ב' מי קתני כו' ולעולם כו':
beur_hagra.en: Set 9 Efi'. Amma Dela 200 and more Dampurushot 20 and 25 in the 22nd name of the Mahari'a.

eliyah_rabbah.he: [ט] אפילו הפרישה מאתמול וכו'. ומשמע אפילו תרומה שהורמה מאמש (בית יוסף), והט"ז תמה הא אי אפשר להפריש תרומה ביום טוב, עד כאן. ולא קשה מידי דהוה אמינא בעבר והפריש קיימא לן דהוי הפרשה, ועוד דבש"ס [ביצה] דף י"ב [י"ג] קאמר רוב תרומה פירש רש"י דיש תרומה מפריש ביום טוב עיין שם ודו"ק, גם מה שהקשה על בית יוסף במה שכתב דהלכה כבית הלל על חלה הא כולי עלמא מודים על כרחך לא דק דלא כתב זה אלא על תרומה ולא על חלה שהרי כתב הבית יוסף תיכף וחלה ומתנות דשרי לכולי עלמא להוליך וכו'. עוד האריך בסוף סימן תקי"ב שהבינו דירושלמי וש"ס דילן פליגי והקשו על בית יוסף וראיה ברורה לזה מאגודה הטיח הרבה על הבית יוסף שהבין דמהרי"א אוסר בזה שהוא נגד הש"ס דף י"ב, ולעניות דעתי יש לומר בש"ס דוקא מה שמותר להפריש ביום טוב הוא דמותר להוליך מתנות הוא אף שהורמו מאתמול כיון שמותר להפריש ביום טוב ומה שמדמה החלה היינו כשלש ביום טוב דמותר להפריש אבל בלש בערב יום טוב דאסור להפריש ביום טוב אף שהפריש בערב יום טוב אסור להוליכו ותרומה דמתיר להוליכה שמיירי כשעבר והפרישו ביום טוב וכדלעיל, מיהו לדינא גם הבית יוסף ושולחן ערוך כתבו דמותר אפילו הפריש מאתמול ועיין בעבודת הקודש דף ל"ט:
eliyah_rabbah.en: [9] Even if he separated it yesterday, etc. And it implies even terumah that was raised last night (Beit Yosef). And the Taz wondered: it is impossible to separate terumah on Yom Tov, until here. And this is no difficulty at all, for I would have thought that if one transgressed and separated, we hold that it is a [valid] separation; and further, in the Gemara [Beitzah] folio 12 [13] it says 'most of terumah'; Rashi explained that there is terumah that one separates on Yom Tov; see there and be precise. Also regarding what he asked upon Beit Yosef in that he wrote that the halachah follows Beit Hillel regarding challah, when everyone agrees: necessarily he was not precise, for he wrote this only regarding terumah and not regarding challah, for Beit Yosef immediately wrote: and challah and gifts, which all permit to bring, etc. Further he prolonged at the end of siman 512, that they understood that the Yerushalmi and our Gemara disagree, and they asked upon Beit Yosef; and a clear proof for this is from Agudah, who strongly attacked Beit Yosef who understood that Mahari Weil forbids in this, which is against the Gemara folio 12. And in my humble opinion one can say: in the Gemara, specifically what is permitted to separate on Yom Tov is what is permitted to bring; gifts are [permitted] even if raised yesterday, since it is permitted to separate on Yom Tov; and what he compares to challah is when one kneads on Yom Tov, when it is permitted to separate; but if one kneaded on erev Yom Tov, when it is forbidden to separate on Yom Tov, even if he separated on erev Yom Tov it is forbidden to bring it; and terumah that he permits to bring, the discussion is where one transgressed and separated it on Yom Tov, as above. However, for the law, Beit Yosef and Shulchan Aruch also wrote that it is permitted even if he separated yesterday; and see Avodas HaKodesh, folio 39.

machatzit_hashekel.he: (ס"ק ט) מן המשויר חלה אבל אסור כו' זה גם בחול אסור כמ"ש הרא"ש דגבי חלה כתיב ראשית לכן בעינן שיהיו שירי' ניכרים דהיינו לאחר שהפריש חלה ישארו שירי'. וכן מבואר בי"ד וכן דייק לשון רמ"א שכ' מפריש מן המשויר. משמע קצת מן המשויר ולא כולו. אולם הרב"י הקשה על הטור שהביא תחלה דעת ר"ח דבחלת ח"ל אפי' לש מעי"ט מותר להפריש חלה בי"ט כיון דאוכל והולך ואח"כ מפריש אין ההפרש' מיקרי תיקון. אבל הרי"ף ורש"י אוסרים. וכ' עוד ור"ח כ' בשם רש"י דאפי' מה שאוכל ומשייר החלה הוי בכלל אין מגביהים תרומות ומעשרות. וכיון דאיכא פלוגתא דרבוותא טוב שלא להפריש אלא אוכל ומשייר עכ"ל הטור. וכתב הרב"י ואע"ג דלר"ח בשם רש"י לאכול ולשייר נמי אסור לא חש רבינו לאותו סברא דחומרא גדולה הוא. ואפשר דתיקון זה שכתב רבינו מהני גם לפי מ"ש ר"ח בשם רש"י כו' דהאי אוכל ומשייר שכ' ר"ח היינו שאוכל כל הפת ומשייר כדי חלה לבד או מעט יותר דה"ל כמפריש ממש ואוכל ומשייר שכתב רבינו היינו שמשייר הרבה יותר מכדי חלה דתו לא הוי כמפריש חלה בי"ט שהרי במוצי"ט מפריש חלה מתוך פת מרובה. והכי דייק לשון רבינו כו' עכ"ל הרב"י. נראה. דתי' בתרא נרא' עיקר בעיני הרב"י. ולפ"ז מי שרוצה לצאת גם ידי הר"ח בשם רש"י צריך להניח הרבה יותר משיעור חלה. אבל הב"ק תולק על הרב"י ומפרש דברי הר"ח בשם רש"י דאוסר אלא לפי שיטת רש"י דס"ל בחול סגי אם מניח רק כדי חלה מצומצם. דס"ל דכה"ג לא בעי' שיהיו שירי' ניכרים. וע"ז כ' דבי"ט אסור כה"ג דזה הוי כהפרשה. אבל לדידן דס"ל כהרא"ש דגם בחול צריך להניח מעט יותר משיעור חלה כנ"ל כה"ג מודה הר"ח בשם רש"י דגם בי"ט מותר דלא נראה כמפריש וא"כ א"ש דברי הטור דאם מניח מעט יותר משיעור חלה יוצא אליבא דכ"ע וא"צ להניח הרבה יותר משיעור חלה:
machatzit_hashekel.en: (s.k. 9) From the remainder — challah; but forbidden, etc. — this is also forbidden on chol, as Ra'ash wrote: regarding challah it is written 'first,' therefore we require recognizable remainder — meaning after separating challah remainder remains. So explained in Yoreh De'ah and Rama inferred 'separates from the remainder' — implies some of the remainder, not all. However Rabbi Yosef challenged Tur who first brought Rashba that for challah of the Diaspora even for Yom Tov need one may separate challah on Yom Tov since he eats and continues and afterward separates — the separation is not called fixing; but Rif and Rashi forbid. He also wrote Rashba in Rashi's name that even what he eats and leaves for challah is included in 'we do not separate terumot and ma'asrot'; since there is a dispute of authorities, better not to separate but eat and leave, end of Tur. Rabbi Yosef wrote: although for Rashba in Rashi's name to eat and leave is also forbidden, our Rabbi did not heed that view as it is a great stringency; and perhaps this fixing our Rabbi wrote helps also per Rashba in Rashi's name, etc.: that 'eat and leave' Rashba means he eats all the dough and leaves only for challah alone or slightly more — that is like actual separating; but 'eat and leave' our Rabbi wrote means he leaves much more than challah measure — then it is not like separating challah on Yom Tov, for on motza'ei Yom Tov one separates challah from much dough. So our Rabbi's wording is inferred, end of Rabbi Yosef. It appears the latter view is primary in Rabbi Yosef's eyes; therefore one who wants to satisfy also Rashba in Rashi's name must leave much more than challah measure. But Pri Megadim challenges Rabbi Yosef and explains Rashba in Rashi's name forbids only per Rashi who holds on chol it suffices if he leaves only minimal challah — he holds then recognizable remainder is not required; and on that basis he wrote on Yom Tov forbidden in such a case as separation. But for us who hold like Ra'ash that even on chol one must leave slightly more than challah measure, in such a case Rashba in Rashi's name admits also on Yom Tov permitted as it does not appear like separating; and if so one need not say Tur's words that if he leaves slightly more than challah measure he satisfies all views and need not leave much more than challah measure.

magen_avraham.he: מותר להפריש. דלא טבלן וא"כ אינו מתקן כלום דמפורשים ועומדות הן דניכרות בפ"ע:
magen_avraham.en: It is permitted to be broken. Dalai Latlan and I do not repair any of the sermons and stand for them:

mishnah_berurah.he: {מב} מותר להפריש המתנות ביו"ט - משום דאינו מתקן דגם קודם הפרשה לא טבלן ועוד דמפורשות ועומדות בגוף הבהמה:
mishnah_berurah.en: (b) The gifts in the U.S. are permitted to be circulated – because Daino is a model before the affair will not be drowned and more sermons and stands in the body of stage:

peri_megadim.he: מותר עט״ז באות ה׳ ולהוליכם לכהן ועפר״ח:
peri_megadim.en: It is permissible to use the 17th letter of the the Master and lead them to serve as priests and Afarah:

turei_zahav.he: מותר להפריש המתנות. הטעם כתבתי בס"ג בשם מהרי"א:
turei_zahav.en: The gifts are allowed. The taste I wrote in a book called Mahari:

kaf_hachayyim.he: ט) שם. אפי' ע"י שינוי. וכמו בכל מלאכות האסורות ביו"ט דאפי' ע"י שינוי אסור וכמ"ש לעיל סי' תצ"ה או' כ"ה יעו"ש:
kaf_hachayyim.en: 9) There. Even in an unusual manner. This follows the rule for all melachos forbidden on Yom Tov, which remain forbidden even when performed in an unusual manner, as written above, siman 495, subsection 25. See there.
